pr_title: Move parameter encoding and validation to `ActionDispatch::Journey::Router`
pr_body:
Closes: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/42278

Parameter encoding and checks to verify whether all encodings are valid are currently done in the [ActionDispatch::Request object](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/168a277bc63f5d40bbb21df1b19fa8f425f992fb/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/request.rb#L397). However, middleware may instantiate a request and access it's parameters. This causes encoding validation to be performed prior to the controller / action being known, resulting in an "invalid parameters" error if any of the parameters are non UTF-8, even if the controller will specify custom encoding or skip parameter encoding.

This PR moves parameter encoding and validation from the request object to the router. Once we're in the router, we have the full context on the controller and action and can properly encode and check the encodings.

To reproduce the bug, one can follow the steps @fxn laid out in the above issue:

```ruby
class FooController < ApplicationController
  skip_parameter_encoding :index
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token

  def index
    head :ok
  end
end

----

class FooMiddleware
  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    request = ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)
    request.params
    @app.call(request.env)
  end
end

---

require "net/http"

uri = URI("http://localhost:3000")
Net::HTTP.post_form(uri, "foo" => "\xe1") # Invalid UTF-8.
# => ActionController::BadRequest (Invalid request parameters: Invalid encoding for parameter: �)
```

Note that the encoding currently being performed in the request object makes things problematic even if parameters are valid UTF-8, because it prevents custom encoding from working. If a controller specifies any sort of custom encoding (per-param encoding as introduced [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40457)), it will not be applied if a piece of middleware touches the request parameters. This is because the `action_dispatch.request.request_parameters` header value will be set on the request the first time around (when the middleware is accessing parameters), and won't have the appropriate controller / action context.

### Summary
- `Request::Utils` still holds the bulk of the logic pertaining to applying parameter encoding + validating whether all parameters have valid encoding
- I've added a `query_params=` setter to `AD::Request` so that we can set this from the router
- The calls to `Request::Utils.set_binary_encoding` and `Request::Utils.check_param_encoding` have been moved to `AD::Journey::Router` - in `AD::Journey::Router#serve` we encode and validate the path params, and then either the query params or the post params depending on the request type

Changes to tests:
- I've removed `actionpack/test/controller/parameter_encoding_test.rb` altogether, since the behaviour being tested ultimately needs to come through the router now. All of the tests that were in this file have been reimplemented in `actionpack/test/dispatch/routing_test.rb`
- I've removed any of the encoding / encoding validation tests from `actionpack/test/dispatch/request_test.rb` and also reimplemented them in `actionpack/test/dispatch/routing_test.rb`.

cc @fxn @jhawthorn @rafaelfranca

issue_context.title: Accessing request.params breaks parameter encoding validation
issue_context.body:
Given a controller:

```ruby
class FooController < ApplicationController
  skip_parameter_encoding :index
  skip_before_action :verify_authenticity_token

  def index
    head :ok
  end
end
```

parameters in the `index` action should be able to carry any payload. For example, this should work

```ruby
require "net/http"

uri = URI("http://localhost:3000")
Net::HTTP.post_form(uri, "foo" => "\xe1") # Invalid UTF-8.
```

and it does.

However, a middleware as innocent as

```ruby
class FooMiddleware
  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    request = ActionDispatch::Request.new(env)
    request.params
    @app.call(request.env)
  end
end
```

interferes somehow with parameter encoding validation, and the request now raises

```
ActionController::BadRequest (Invalid request parameters: Invalid encoding for parameter: �)
```
comments:
Some progress.

The mere evaluation of `request.params` in the middleware, [triggers](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/168a277bc63f5d40bbb21df1b19fa8f425f992fb/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/parameters.rb#L55) the invocation of `AD::Request#request_parameters`, which [performs encoding validation](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/168a277bc63f5d40bbb21df1b19fa8f425f992fb/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/request.rb#L397).

However, since we have not reached the router yet, that code does not even have the information needed to do encoding validation. For example, you do not know the controller. The exception is raised by the middleware itself.

/cc @jhawthorn
Possibly this changed in https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40124 ?

I have not bisected, but that patch seems like a good candidate.

My thoughts:

1. Instantiating `AD::Request` in middleware to access and/or modify `env` is normal.
2. In particular, users should be able to access `request.params`, and the implementation with its cache invalidation, etc. suggest to me this is expected.

I believe we agree on that, no?

So, since parameter encoding validation depends on controller/action, from a logical point of view it does not make sense that we perform any parameter encoding validation before reaching the router.

Maybe that means the router is the one that has to validate the parameters somehow, cannot be embedded/automated in the request object like it is now.

Not sure if we need to guarantee valid encodings above the router, if not, maybe the fix is moving things down. If yes, the design is not good, you just lack the necessary information.

Let's cc @adrianna-chang-shopify and @rafaelfranca.

Hey @fxn !

Can confirm that https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40124 is likely the candidate (although validating the encoding on the request object was first introduced [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/21990) to catch invalid querystring values, with https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40124 simply extending that to `POST` requests).

Accessing `request.params` in a piece of middleware should certainly be doable, so it makes sense on my end to push this down to the router. Maybe `AD::Journey::Router#serve` could handle all of the encoding / validations ? I don't see a reason to need to validate encodings prior to hitting the router, but maybe @rafaelfranca has some extra context on that 😄

Perfect @adrianna-chang-shopify! 

Another option could be somewhere near [`ActionDispatch::Routing::RouteSet#call`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/328113b0adfb516639ea0ad9845e15877b8c8141/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/routing/route_set.rb#L838-L842), or [`ActionDispatch::Routing::RouteSet::Dispatcher#serve`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/328113b0adfb516639ea0ad9845e15877b8c8141/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/routing/route_set.rb#L28-L39) since that seems to be the [lowest boundary](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/routing/route_set.rb#L32) before passing the request to the controller (if my limited understanding of this part of the framework is right). Though the dispatcher should probably stay at dispatching only.

Let's see what @rafaelfranca says!
Nah, can't be in `AD::Routing::RouteSet#call`, controller and action are set indeed in `AD::Journey::Router#serve`. Yeah, your suggestion is probably the best one.
Great! I should have some time to fix this later in the week, unless you'd like to tackle it @fxn ?
@adrianna-chang-shopify fantastic! all yours!

To give you a concrete example: This issue originated in a middleware stack above a SendGrid webhook.

SendGrid sends email metadata, and params that tell you their encoding. So, you truly can't assume anything before reaching the controller.

@rafaelfranca and I had a chat about this and we've decided to move the [encoding into the controller](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/main/actionpack/lib/action_controller/metal.rb#L200), with `AD::Request` using binary encoding. I'll update the PR I opened to move the encoding from the router into the controller and ensure we've documented the fact that encoding with `AD::Request` is binary since the controller context might not be available yet.
Fantastic @adrianna-chang-shopify!
Happy to test this, we too are seeing issue with processing binary params from Sendgrid's inbound parse API.

Finally had some time to dig into this a bit more, and if I'm not mistaken ensuring that params accessible in middleware are binary encoded will require an upstream change to Rack. Wanted to check in with some smart folks to make sure this all seems sensible before proceeding 😄 

For POST requests, we parse the query parameters [here](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/d0c6efc666ede26768f33935f00530629690369a/lib/rack/request.rb#L448), and for GET requests we parse them [here](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/master/lib/rack/request.rb#L424). Both end up calling [`parse_query`](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/d0c6efc666ede26768f33935f00530629690369a/lib/rack/request.rb#L579-L581), which calls `query_parser.parse_nested_query`:

```ruby
# lib/rack/query_parser.rb
    def parse_nested_query(qs, separator = nil)
      params = make_params

      unless qs.nil? || qs.empty?
        (qs || '').split(separator ? (COMMON_SEP[separator] || /[#{separator}] */n) : DEFAULT_SEP).each do |p|
          k, v = p.split('=', 2).map! { |s| unescape(s) } # THIS LINE IS IMPORTANT

          normalize_params(params, k, v, param_depth_limit)
        end
      end

      return params.to_h
    rescue ArgumentError => e
      raise InvalidParameterError, e.message, e.backtrace
    end
```

When splitting the query string we use [`unescape`](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/d0c6efc666ede26768f33935f00530629690369a/lib/rack/utils.rb#L53), which forces a UTF-8 encoding, meaning that when we access params in `AD::Request`, they are already encoded as UTF-8.

My proposition:
- `Rack::QueryParser#parse_query` takes an [`unescaper` block](https://github.com/rack/rack/blob/d0c6efc666ede26768f33935f00530629690369a/lib/rack/query_parser.rb#L35), allowing a custom method to be used for unescaping the query string
- We could adapt `Rack::QueryParser#parse_nested_query` to do the same
- This would allow us to override `#parse_query` in `AD::Request` and call `#query_parser.parse_nested_query` with an `unescape` method that ensures the encoding is binary (ie. `Rack::Utils.unescape(s, Encoding::ASCII_8BIT)`)

Does this make sense? cc @jhawthorn @fxn @rafaelfranca

We could change Rack but that would require Rails to force people to upgrade rack and I'd like to avoid that. We don't need to change the encoding of the parameters,  but we should move the validation of the encoding to the controller. It will be up to the middleware to check if the parameters they have are using a valid encoding.
